diagram_math_checks.justification: Definition lines 39–40 give f_{i,n}: X_i^n -> [M_i]; supplier def-it-finite-iid-multisource defines terminal i observing X_i^n. The two displayed input arrows go only from X_1^n to f_{1,n} and from X_k^n to f_{k,n}. No cross-source arrow or inter-encoder message appears.

Each encoder output wire is labeled m_i in [M_i], with caption m_i=f_{i,n}(X_i^n) and cardinality M_i. This is consistent with the exact fixed-length rate n^{-1} ln M_i at line 43; no alphabet product is incorrectly attributed to an individual encoder.

Line 42 defines g_n on the full product of all k message alphabets with output in the product of k reproduction-block alphabets. Caption states the input is (m_1,...,m_k); the output wire is the tuple (hat X_1^n,...,hat X_k^n), with its exact product codomain stated at line 70. Separate input wires represent tuple assembly, not maps from a single factor into a product.

All five displayed arrows point left to right: each displayed source to its encoder, each encoder to the common decoder, and the decoder to its tuple output. First/last branches are distinct because k>=2. Caption specifies the intermediate branches when k>2; ellipses assert no extra terminal when k=2. The final sentence explicitly allows correlations under the original joint law, avoiding an independence claim.

The full Definition lines 37–43 and original Remarks line 47 remain unchanged. The figure is expository, outside any Facts/proof section; no proof is supplied by this definition item and no rigorous argument relies on the figure.
